title: Star-delta starter
summary: Start a motor in star to cut the starting current to a third, then change to delta on a timer, with interlocks so star and delta never close together.

why.text:
Extract fan **EF-2** at the fictional Riverside plant has a 5.5 kW motor. Started direct-on-line it would pull around six times its full-load current, dip the supply and upset other equipment on the same board.

A star-delta starter starts the motor in [[star]] at about a third of the DOL current, then switches to [[delta]] for full power once it is up to speed.

cards.title: The idea
cards.text:
Use a **400 V Δ / 690 V Y** motor on a 400 V supply. Its normal running connection is delta.

- **Start in star**: each winding gets 230 V instead of 400 V. Starting current and starting torque both fall to **one third** of DOL.
- **Run in delta**: after a few seconds, when the motor is near full speed, change to delta for full torque.

Because torque is only a third in star, star-delta suits loads that start light: fans, centrifugal pumps, unloaded compressors.

cards.title: Three contactors
cards.text:
- **KM1 main** feeds L1, L2, L3 to U1, V1, W1 through the overload.
- **KM2 star** joins W2, U2 and V2 together (the star point).
- **KM3 delta** connects W2 to L1, U2 to L2 and V2 to L3.

Start: KM1 + KM2. Run: KM1 + KM3. The motor needs six cables from the starter, not three.

cards.title: Star and delta must never overlap
cards.text:
KM2 joins W2, U2, V2. KM3 puts three different phases on those same terminals. Both in together joins all three phases: a short circuit.

So each coil goes through the other one's NC contact: **KM3 21-22** feeds KM2, **KM2 21-22** feeds KM3. Star-delta contactor sets usually have a mechanical interlock between KM2 and KM3 as well.

cards.title: The timer
cards.text:
An [[on-delay timer]] **KT** starts timing when START is pressed:
- **15-16** (delayed opening, NC) feeds KM2 star. It opens when the time is up.
- **17-18** (delayed closing, NO) feeds KM3 delta. It closes when the time is up.

KM2 drops out first; only then can KM3 pull in through KM2 21-22. Set the time so the motor is close to full speed at changeover. Too short and you get a large current surge at changeover; too long and the motor works in star with too little torque.

cards.title: Setting the overload
cards.text:
Here F2 is between KM1 and U1, V1, W1, so it carries the **winding** current, not the line current. In delta, winding current = line current ÷ √3.

So set it to **0.58 × FLC**. For this 10.7 A motor: 10.7 × 0.58 ≈ **6.2 A**. Setting it to 10.7 A would leave the motor unprotected.

If an overload is fitted in the supply line instead, set it to full FLC. Always check where it is on the drawing.

cards.title: Six cables, six terminals to prove dead
cards.text:
A star-delta motor has two sets of cables. When you isolate, prove dead at **all six** motor terminals (and earth), not just U1, V1, W1.

Insulation test both sets of cables and the motor, with the starter isolated and the links (if any) removed.

show.intro: This star-delta starter is wired correctly. Watch the current fall in star, and the order KM2 out, then KM3 in.

tasks.text: Press **START (S1)**. KM1 and KM2 pull in: the motor starts in star. Note the current: about 2 × FLC, not 6 ×.
While it is in star, measure across one winding, **U1 to U2**, in V~. About 230 V.
Wait for the timer. KM2 drops out, then KM3 pulls in: the motor runs in delta.
Measure **U1 to U2** again. In delta each winding now has the full 400 V.
Look at F2: in delta it carries the winding current (about 6.2 A), not the 10.7 A line current, so it does not heat up. Press **STOP (S0)**.

checks.fail: KM2 (star) and KM3 (delta) were energised at the same time. That short-circuits the supply through the motor terminals. Put KM3 21-22 in the KM2 coil circuit, and KM2 21-22 in the KM3 coil circuit.
A protective device tripped as soon as power was applied. Look for a wire joining two phases, or + to 0 V.
The circuit will not settle (relay chatter).
KM1 pulls in without anyone pressing START.
START does not pull in and hold the main contactor KM1. Trace G1 + through S0, F2 95-96, S1 (with KM1 13-14 in parallel) to KM1 A1, then A2 to 0 V.
The star contactor KM2 does not pull in at start. It is fed through KT 15-16 (closed while timing) and KM3 21-22.
The delta contactor KM3 is in at the start. It must wait for the timer (KT 17-18).
At start the motor is not in star. KM2 must join W2, U2 and V2 so each winding gets 230 V.
The timer KT has not run out. Its coil must be fed from the START circuit, after S1 and the holding contact.
KM2 (star) did not drop out when the timer ran out. Feed it through the delayed-opening contact KT 15-16.
KM3 (delta) did not pull in after the timer. Feed it through KT 17-18 and KM2 21-22.
After changeover the windings are not in delta. KM3 must connect W2 to L1, U2 to L2 and V2 to L3.
After changeover the motor is not running forward.
A protective device tripped at changeover. Check the delta wiring: W2 to L1, U2 to L2, V2 to L3.
F2 tripped in normal running. It sits in the winding circuit, so it carries FLC ÷ √3: set it to 0.58 × FLC.
STOP does not drop out KM1.
STOP does not drop out KM3.

guided.intro: The power circuit, START/STOP and the holding contact are wired. **Wire the coils, the timer and the interlocks.**
hints: Everything starts from S1:14 (after START and the holding contact): wire it to KM1:A1, KT:A1, KT:15 and KT:17.
Star path: KT:16 to KM3:21 (delta's NC interlock), then KM3:22 to KM2:A1.
Delta path: KT:18 to KM2:21 (star's NC interlock), then KM2:22 to KM3:A1.
All four A2 terminals (KM1, KT, KM2, KM3) return to G1 − (0 V).

unguided.intro: Now wire the **delta and star contactor power circuits** (including the star point) and **all the coils, timer and interlocks**, with no hints.

break.intro: This star-delta starter has **one hidden fault**. Start it, watch the sequence and the event log, then find the cause by measuring. Some faults take a while to show: watch the overload heat. In this simulator you may measure voltage with the power on. On a real panel, live testing is only allowed when it is justified, by a competent person, following the site risk assessment and GS38. Switch off Q1 before any Ω test.

faults.report: Timer contact KT 15-16 is stuck closed: the motor never leaves star, and the overload eventually trips.
Timer contact KT 17-18 never closes: star drops out but delta never comes in.
The star contactor's interlock contact KM2 21-22 is open: delta cannot pull in.
Delta wiring error: KM3 terminal 4 goes to V2 instead of U2.
The KM2 (star) coil is open circuit.

extraReports: Nothing is wrong with the starter.

questions.text: Compared with DOL, the starting current in star is about…
questions.explain: Each winding gets 1/√3 of the voltage and the line current is 1/√3 of the delta line current again: 1/3 overall.

questions.text: Compared with DOL, the starting torque in star is about…
options: One third, so the load must start light
questions.explain: Torque falls with current. Star-delta suits fans and pumps, not loads that start heavy.

questions.text: The supply is 400 V. Which motor is suitable for star-delta starting?
questions.explain: In delta a 230 V Δ / 400 V Y motor would get 400 V per winding and burn out. Star-delta needs windings rated 400 V in delta.

questions.text: Why must KM2 (star) and KM3 (delta) never be closed together?
options: It joins all three phases through the motor terminals: a short circuit
questions.explain: KM2 joins W2, U2, V2; KM3 puts L1, L2, L3 on them. Both together is a three-phase short. Interlocks prevent it.

questions.text: F2 is wired between KM1 and U1, V1, W1. The motor FLC is 10.7 A. What should F2 be set to?
questions.explain: There it carries winding current, which in delta is line current ÷ √3.

questions.text: The timer is set far too short. What happens?
options: Changeover happens at low speed with a large current surge
questions.explain: In delta at low speed the motor draws nearly DOL current, so the benefit of star starting is lost.

questions.text: The starter never leaves star. What happens if the fan runs like this?
options: It runs weak and draws too much current under load until the overload trips
questions.explain: In star the motor has only about a third of its torque. Under load the current rises above the winding rating.

questions.text: You need to work on the motor of a star-delta drive. Where do you prove dead?
options: At all six motor terminals and to earth, after isolating and locking off
questions.explain: A star-delta motor has two sets of cables; either set could be live from a separate contactor.

apply.intro: Do this on the training bench while your trainer watches. Your trainer signs it off. An app score alone never makes anyone competent or authorised.

items.text: Carries out safe isolation and proves dead at all six motor terminals.
Checks the nameplate is 400 V Δ and removes any links from the terminal box.
Wires the main, star and delta contactors, the star point, the timer and both electrical interlocks to the drawing; fits the mechanical interlock where supplied.
Sets the overload to 0.58 × FLC (when fitted in the winding circuit) and explains why.
Carries out continuity and insulation resistance tests on both sets of motor cables and records them.
Functional test with the trainer: star start, timed changeover, no overlap of star and delta, STOP, overload trip, no automatic restart.
